# Episode rules: titans_from_zero (v3, final)

**Question.** Strip ten famous fortunes down to what is inside their heads and take away every lender: was their money ever skill, or was it luck?  
**Angle.** credit is the hidden variable: people who can build or sell with their own hands recover, people whose deals ran on other people's trust stall, and the real winner is the one who bought a small piece of everyone for forty dollars  
**Beyond a summary.** it is not a list of billionaire origin stories: it is an invented controlled experiment (same start, no credit) that isolates one mechanism, trust as capital, and lets the viewer watch it decide outcomes  
**Tone / arc.** dry, fast situational comedy with real stakes; a documentary of events happening now (D-61) / schadenfreude on the bench, curiosity at the first hustles, dread as the promise of 500 outruns the parts, shock at the fire, respect at Belfort's refusal, satisfaction at the honest win, and a twist that reframes everything  
**Stakes / payoff.** riders' safety and the heroes' last dollar against a buyer offering riches for silence / luck decided which envelope paid; skill decided who was still standing when it did, and the man who never built anything owns a piece of eight of them

Jurisdictions: US, GE (US: YouTube's operator, the main market (D-52) and the residence of most of the people depicted; GE: the creator's residence (confirmed 2026-10-17, ES-15). Kevin O'Leary is Canadian; Canada is not a named market, so no Canadian rule is applied (noted as a gap).)

| RK-19 | The garage fire (S11) and a sitting president in a comedy (advertiser suitability) | PASS | A non-graphic property fire with no injuries and a politics-free comedy are not the content those guidelines restrict; no material issue found. |
| RK-20 | The invented lines of seven real people (Trump, Musk, Belfort, O'Leary, Kiyosaki, Cuban, Bezos), told as short quotes by the one narrator in his own voice (D-68) and as speech bubbles in the Shorts (D-62) | PASS | A drawn speech bubble over a caricature is the oldest form of satirical cartoon and cannot be taken for a recording of the person, so moving the lines from a voice to bubbles removes the provider-terms problem without adding a new one. No material issue found, provided the bubble texts stay the approved lines (ER-02) and contain no political content (ER-08). Under D-68 the same holds for the narrator's told quotes: V-51 bars synthesizing a living person's voice or likeness, and a narrator reporting invented words in his own voice is neither; the description's notice (ER-06) still says every line is invented. |

Disclosure required: no (Fully drawn 2D animation of an obviously invented situation; no photograph, footage or realistic rendering of any real person; the only synthetic voices are the narrator and the invented Vance, and the real people speak in drawn speech bubbles (D-62). YouTube lists fantasy and fully animated content as not requiring the label (14328491, re-read 2026-10-20). If a picture, thumbnail or Short of a real person could pass as a photograph, the label becomes required (ER-01).)
